chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Al-Hijr, and he was seated, and with him were a number of his family members, so I heard him saying: 'My teeth hurt, so I took the cyperus and rubbed it by my teeth, and that benefitted me, and it settled down from me.'

key_terms.السُّعْد: The suda (a plant, likely saltwort or cyperus)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Hasan al-Askari use to treat his toothache?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam Al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him), demonstrating the prophetic tradition of using natural remedies like saltwort (suda) for dental care. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imams' holistic guidance, where spiritual authority is complemented by tangible, health-preserving practices relevant to daily life.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad who said,

‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> in Al Hijr (at the Kabah), and he<sup>asws</sup> was seated, and with him<sup>asws</sup> were a number of his<sup>asws</sup> family members, so I hear him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My teeth hurt, so I took the cyperus and rubbed it down by my teeth, and that benefitted me, and settled down from it’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad who has said the following:

“I once saw abu al-Hassan sitting in al-Hijr (near al-Ka‘bah) along with a group of his family members and I heard him saying, ‘I had a toothache so I took cyperus and rubbed with it my teeth, it benefited me and the pain calmed down.’” End of the Book of Foods followed by the Book of Drinks, by the will of Allah, and all praise belongs to Allah alone, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause."
